Apple last week launched what could be described as its first batch of AI-powered wearables, including the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Both products feature a new “Audio Intelligence” capability that works in tandem with Siri AI. However, a report today from Bloomberg indicates that another AI product widely rumoured on the market — a wearable pendant — has been shelved.

Apple’s AI wearables roadmap includes a pendant project that, at least for now, will not be moving forward.

The AI era has spurred plenty of software innovation, but has yet to truly translate into an entirely new product category.

Of course, the industry has made attempts — the Humane Ai Pin, for instance, ended in failure. Meta’s AI smart glasses have also had some success, though that market remains quite niche.

There have been rumours that Apple is developing multiple AI-centric wearables. The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 launched last week can be considered the first products to hit the market.

But according to Bloomberg journalist Mark Gurman, the company had also been working on a wearable pendant equipped with a camera. However, development on that product now appears to have stalled.

Earlier this year, Gurman reported that the pendant would “serve as a camera always-on for the iPhone, with a built-in microphone for Siri input.”

Now Apple seems to have decided to shelve the project. Instead, the company is focusing on baking AI features into the Apple Watch, while also developing next-generation AirPods with built-in cameras, as well as smart glasses slated for release in 2027.

How AI will weave into new products remains unclear, but Gurman also noted that Apple is working on a brand-new screen-less wearable focused on health monitoring, in an effort to compete more effectively with WHOOP.

Would you be interested in getting your hands on an AI pendant designed by Apple? Let us know in the comments.
